sections.h2: Selling a house in Egg Harbor Township, NJ
sections.html:
Egg Harbor Township is a large Atlantic County municipality, 75.47 square miles of which 67.05 is land, and it is separate from Egg Harbor City. About 48,435 people live here. Owner-occupancy is high at 84.4 percent, the median owner-occupied home value is $312,700, and median household income is $97,190.

Because most houses here are owned rather than rented, the sale is usually a household moving on, and the one task to line up before closing is the state fire-safety certificate.

New Jersey's Division of Fire Safety runs an online smoke certification application with "Change of Ownership" as a stated reason, and it asks for the closing date, block, lot and whether you are the seller or the buyer's representative. Sheriff's sales, foreclosures, forfeitures and purchases from a federal agency work differently: the new owner must obtain the certificate before moving in. A building that is uninhabitable and will be rehabilitated or demolished can be exempt from the certificate, but it cannot be occupied until a new certificate of occupancy comes from the local construction official.

For the township's own form, fee and timing, call the Bureau of Fire Inspections before you set a closing date.

The population rose 1.2 percent from the April 2020 base of 47,849 to 48,435. There are 17,261 households averaging 2.78 people, and 93.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low and a well-priced house tends to draw local move-up households. Owners with a paid-off house pay far less each month than renters, which is why some heirs think twice before selling at all.

Median owner costs run $2,371 a month with a mortgage and $954 without one, and median gross rent is $1,456. That gap between owning and renting matters if you are deciding whether to keep an inherited house as a rental.

The township is one of 56 South Jersey municipalities in the Pinelands National Reserve, and part of it lies in the state-designated Pinelands Area. The Pinelands Commission classed Egg Harbor Township, Hamilton and Galloway as Regional Growth Areas, which steered residential construction into these towns so the preserved Pine Barrens could keep its trees.

  • If your lot sits near wetlands or protected land, ask the township's construction office about limits before planning a deck, shed or addition.
  • If a past owner added anything without a permit, a buyer's attorney may ask about it, so locate the paperwork first. Heirs selling an older home should look for old permits in the estate files.
  • Name the section of the township in your listing. The seat of government is in Bargaintown, and the township includes Cardiff, English Creek, Farmington, Scullville, Steelmanville and West Atlantic City.

sections.h2: Roads, buses and what draws buyers
sections.html:
The Atlantic City Expressway crosses the township for 5.3 miles and meets the Garden State Parkway at Interchange 7, which is Parkway Interchange 38. Routes 40, 322 and 9 plus county routes 559, 563, 575 and 585 carry local traffic. NJ Transit buses 502, 507, 508 and 509 link the township with Atlantic City, and Atlantic City International Airport lies mostly in the northern part. Mean travel to work is 23.3 minutes. Harbor Square, once the Shore Mall, is the regional shopping center, and the Atlantic County Bikeway runs 7.5 miles from it toward Hamilton Township.

  • Malibu Beach Wildlife Management Area covers 95.7 acres of marsh, dunes and back-bay shoreline and is known locally as Dog Beach, one of the few New Jersey beaches that permits dogs.
  • Storybook Land, a 20 acre children's park, opened in 1955 on the township's mainland side.
  • The township borders Ocean City and has Great Egg Harbor Bay shoreline in its eastern segment.

Name the nearest of these in your listing, since they are what a buyer from outside Atlantic County will recognize. Egg Harbor Township Schools run seven schools for pre-kindergarten through grade 12, with Egg Harbor Township High School at the top. Families moving in from elsewhere in the county often ask which school their street feeds, so call the district and put the answer in your listing before the first showing.

sections.h2: State transfer fees on a typical sale
sections.html:
At a median value of $312,700, a typical township sale lands in the state's lower schedule, the one for deals up to $350,000.

New Jersey realty transfer fee, standard sale up to $350,000
Price bandRate per $500
$0 to $150,000$2.00
$150,000 to $200,000$3.35
$200,000 to $350,000$3.90

Sellers who are seniors, blind or disabled, and sales of low or moderate income housing, can claim a partial exemption on Form RTF-1.

sections.h2: How to appeal an assessment in Atlantic County
sections.html: Atlantic County's Board of Taxation sits in Mays Landing at 5909 Main Street and can be reached at (609) 645-5820. Petitions are due by April 1. Hearings usually take place from April through September at the Historic Courthouse. The board mails a hearing notice at least ten days ahead, and any comparable sales you rely on must reach the board, the municipal assessor and the municipal clerk at least seven days before the hearing. Comparables should be genuine sales in the same town during the year before the prior October 1. Most foreclosures, sheriff's sales, estate sales and short sales are treated as not usable. A reduction comes back as a credit through a revised bill from the tax collector, and you have 45 days from the judgment to go to the State Tax Court.

On the deed, a seller who lives in New Jersey signs GIT/REP-3, while one who lives elsewhere signs GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless a listed assurance fits. Your attorney or title agent normally handles the recording, so the practical job for you is to supply the smoke certificate, payoff letters and any permit paperwork early.

Here is a quick order of operations: submit the state smoke certification application once the closing date is known, call the township fire bureau about its form and fee, collect payoff figures, then let your attorney schedule the closing. A cash buyer skips the appraisal and lender review, but the certificate and the deed work stay.

If the property was bought at a sheriff's sale or foreclosure, remember the rule runs the other way: the new owner obtains the certificate before moving in. If the building is uninhabitable, ask the local construction official before you list, because it cannot be occupied again until a new certificate of occupancy is issued. In every case, keep copies of the smoke certificate, the closing date you gave the state and the block and lot numbers, since the buyer's side may ask for them.

faqs.q: Is Egg Harbor Township the same as Egg Harbor City?
faqs.a: No. They are separate municipalities. This page covers the township, which has about 48,435 residents.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Egg Harbor Township?
faqs.a: Yes, a change of ownership calls for a state smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. Ask the township's Bureau of Fire Inspections for its form, fee and timing before you pick a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Egg Harbor Township?
faqs.a: $312,700 for owner-occupied homes, and 84.4 percent of homes are owner occupied.

faqs.q: When is the Atlantic County tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the tax year, filed with the Atlantic County Board of Taxation. Where a revaluation was done, the deadline is May 1.

faqs.q: How far ahead are Atlantic County hearing notices sent?
faqs.a: At least ten days before the hearing. Comparable sales evidence is due to the board, the assessor and the clerk at least seven days before.
